newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola falls in line with lower CBOT soy.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola falls in line with lower CBOT soy.

text.p: WCE canola futures sagged early in line with weaker CBOT soybeans and farmer selling, traders said. "Hedges are hitting the pit," one trader said.
At 1104 CDT, November canola was bid at $438.30 a tonne, down $1.70 and January canola was bid at $442.00, off $1.60.
Commercials were playing both sides of the flax market. "Farmer selling has been limited so we are not going to be down that far," the trader added.
October flax was unchanged, asked at $398.50.

Weather appeared not to be a determining factor. "They are talking about fairly decent frost over the weekend all across the western Canadian prairies but most of the crops are mature, so they can withstand the weather," he said.
But some rain on Wednesday and Thursday hindered harvesting of feedgrains and oilseeds, he said.
Western barley slipped in fairly slow trade. "There is commercial buying along with local short covering ahead of Canadian Wheat Board Pool Return Outlook Report (today)," another trader said.
November western barley was off $0.80 at $149.50 while October feedwheat firmed $0.20, asked at $201.50 in lackluster trading. The rest of the board was down $0.60 to $1.50.
(All values in Canadian dollars except for feed peas and barley in US dollars).
